Create a polished, working CHIP-8 emulator and visual debugger in one self-contained file: chip8_anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5_01.html.

Use inline HTML, CSS and JavaScript only: no libraries, CDNs, external assets, backend or network requests. It must work offline via file://. Every control must work and every displayed value must reflect real emulator state.

1. EMULATOR CORE

Implement 4096 writable memory bytes, the standard 80-byte font at 0x050, ROM loading at 0x200, sixteen 8-bit registers V0-VF, 16-bit I and PC, a 16-entry return stack, DT/ST timers, a 64x32 framebuffer and 16-key input. Support self-modifying code.

Implement all 34 executable base CHIP-8 patterns:
00E0, 00EE, 1NNN, 2NNN, 3XNN, 4XNN, 5XY0, 6XNN, 7XNN,
8XY0, 8XY1, 8XY2, 8XY3, 8XY4, 8XY5, 8XY6, 8XY7, 8XYE,
9XY0, ANNN, BNNN, CXNN, DXYN, EX9E, EXA1, FX07, FX0A,
FX15, FX18, FX1E, FX29, FX33, FX55, FX65.

Recognize legacy SYS 0NNN, often counted as instruction 35; report it as unsupported after decoding 00E0/00EE. Do not emulate native COSMAC 1802 routines or add partial SUPER-CHIP/XO-CHIP support.

Decode exact patterns: 5XY1 and 9XY1 are invalid. Handle carry, no-borrow including equality, shifted-out bits, BCD and inclusive V0-VX transfers correctly. Capture operands before writes; write arithmetic/shift results before VF. Test X=F, Y=F and X=Y. Capture sprite coordinates before clearing VF. 7XNN does not separately modify VF.

2. COMPATIBILITY AND TIMING

Use these explicit default compatibility settings:
- Shifts use VX; FX55/65 preserve I; BNNN uses NNN+V0.
- Logic operations do not separately reset VF.
- Drawing starts at coordinates modulo 64/32, then clips at right/bottom edges.
- FX1E wraps I to 16 bits and leaves VF unchanged.
- FX29 uses 0x050 + 5*(VX & 0x0F).
- FX0A waits for a fresh keydown, ignoring previously held keys and repeats.
- DXY0 draws nothing and sets VF=0; no vertical-blank drawing wait.

Reset restores original ROM and full machine state while preserving UI prefs and valid breakpoints.

OPCODES (exactly these 34 plus SYS 0NNN recognized as unsupported after 00E0/00EE decode): 00E0 clear, 00EE return (underflow fault), 1NNN jump, 2NNN call (overflow fault at 16), 3XNN, 4XNN, 5XY0 (5XY1 invalid), 6XNN, 7XNN (no VF change), 8XY0, 8XY1, 8XY2, 8XY3, 8XY4 (carry VF after writing VX), 8XY5 (VF=1 if VX>=VY, no borrow, write result before VF), 8XY6 (shift VX source by default, VF=old LSB, write before VF), 8XY7 (VF=1 if VY>=VX), 8XYE (VF=old MSB), 8XY0-3 do not reset VF by default unless compatibility setting enabled, 9XY0 (9XY1 invalid), ANNN, BNNN (NNN+V0), CXNN (seeded deterministic RNG option), DXYN (start at VX%64, VY%32, clip at right/bottom edges, XOR, VF=1 if any lit pixel becomes unlit, capture coords before clearing VF, N=0 draws nothing and VF=0), EX9E, EXA1, FX07, FX0A (waits for fresh keydown, ignores held keys and repeats, does not advance PC until a key is released after pressing; logs once on completion), FX15, FX18, FX1E (wrap I to 16 bits, VF unchanged), FX29 (0x050+5*(VX&0xF)), FX33 BCD at I..I+2 with range validation, FX55/FX65 inclusive V0..VX, preserve I by default with optional increment-by-X+1 or X compat setting. Validate full transfer range before writing. Writes capture operands before modifying registers.

COMPATIBILITY SETTINGS (switchable only while paused, displayed as active): shift source VX (default) or VY; FX55/65 I preserved (default) or incremented; logic ops VF reset (default off) or reset; sprite clipping (default clip) or wrap. Show active settings.

TIMING: CPU runs using elapsed-time accumulators (not per animation frame), speed slider 60-6000 instr/s plus numeric input, default 600. DT and ST decrement at 60 Hz independently while running, including during FX0A waits. Pause freezes CPU and timers. Single Step executes one instruction without advancing timers. Auto-pause when document becomes hidden and discard background elapsed time. Web Audio quiet square/sine beep only while running with ST>0; mute, volume slider, visual activity indicator; init AudioContext after user gesture; silence on pause and fault.

DISPLAY: canvas 64x32 framebuffer scaled with nearest-neighbor at 2:1 aspect; scale/fit controls, optional pixel grid, green/amber/monochrome palettes, optional scanlines, fullscreen button where supported, framebuffer PNG export via canvas.toBlob or toDataURL. Effects never alter emulation state.

DEBUGGER PANELS: header, top transport bar with ROM info (filename, size, address range 0x200-end), status badge (PAUSED/RUNNING/WAITING/BREAKPOINT/FAULT), Run, Pause, Single Step, Reset, Load ROM button with file picker, Load Demo, drag-and-drop loading. Large display beside registers and stack. Registers panel: V0-VF in hex and decimal, highlight VF distinctly, highlight changed values after each step; I, PC, SP/stack depth, DT, ST, instruction count, next opcode. Registers and timers editable with validation while paused. Stack panel shows all 16 entries with active slots, top marker, return addresses; clicking an address navigates disassembly. Disassembly panel: address, raw bytes (actual byte pair at PC even at odd addresses), mnemonic, operands, brief explanation; PC marked as NEXT instruction, last executed marked separately; Follow PC toggle; go-to-address input; branch/call target display; breakpoint gutter click to toggle; invalid instructions marked with note that linear disassembly can interpret sprite data as code and does not recover original source. Memory panel: hex dump of all 4096 bytes, 16 bytes per row with ASCII column, go-to-address, jump-to-PC and jump-to-I, distinct markers for PC, I, font and ROM regions, highlight writes from latest step including unchanged-value writes, validated byte editing while paused. Sprite preview: 8 pixels wide from I or a selected address, height 1-15, byte values shown, safe end-of-memory handling. Breakpoint list with add/remove. Trace panel: ring buffer of last 200 completed instructions with sequence, previous PC, opcode/mnemonic, resulting PC, register changes, memory writes, stack-depth changes; clear and follow-latest controls. Panels reflow for mobile with internal table scrolling, visible focus outlines, clear labels. Throttle refresh while running; update fully after pause, step, edits.

BREAKPOINTS: stop BEFORE executing the instruction at the address. Resuming bypasses the breakpoint at the current PC once; later visits honored. Single Step executes through a breakpoint without removing it.

INPUT: 16-key keypad shown with virtual and physical labels: 1 2 3 C -> 1 2 3 4; 4 5 6 D -> Q W E R; 7 8 9 E -> A S D F; A 0 B F -> Z X C V. Use KeyboardEvent.code (Digit1, Digit2, Digit3, Digit4, KeyQ, KeyW, KeyE, KeyR, KeyA, KeyS, KeyD, KeyF, KeyZ, KeyX, KeyC, KeyV). Handle press and release and simultaneous keys. Mouse and touch keypad with pointer capture and pointercancel handling. Combine keyboard and pointer sources correctly. Clear all held keys on window blur. Do not intercept keys typed in input/textarea/contenteditable/select.

DEMO ROM: embed as a byte array in JS with annotated assembly comments, fully executed by CHIP-8 instructions (no JS animation). Interactive sprite demo: movement with keys 2/4/6/8 with visible physical bindings (W/A/S/D style labels or the mapped keys shown), XOR erase and redraw, DT-paced movement delay, a real CALL/RET drawing subroutine, key-triggered ST beep, an FX0A start interaction, and movement that reaches screen edges demonstrating clipping or wrapping. Demo starts loaded and paused.

FAULTS: detect unknown opcodes, invalid fetches (PC odd or out of range), out-of-bounds memory access, stack overflow and underflow, invalid writes. Never silently wrap addresses into RAM. Fault pauses execution, silences audio, preserves state, and shows faulting address, opcode, and explanation.

SELF-TESTS: Run Self-tests button creates isolated Chip8 instances and checks: arithmetic and flag edge cases (carry, no-borrow at equality, X=F, Y=F, X=Y cases), shifts with source switching, skips, CALL/RET, stack underflow/overflow, BCD, register transfers and I preservation, compatibility switches, XOR collision, input waits for FX0A, timer ticks, invalid operations (5XY1, 9XY1), reset after self-modification. Use a deterministic seeded PRNG for CXNN tests. Show expected vs observed for each test, pass/fail totals, without changing the user session.

KEEP CODE ORGANIZED with camelCase class and method names, clear sections, comments in English. Avoid unbounded loops and avoid rebuilding all memory and disassembly per instruction. The file must be a single HTML document that is complete and functional."}
